title: Voice assistant for developers on Mac: explain errors and talk prompts into Cursor
metaTitle: Voice assistant for developers on Mac
description: A voice assistant for developers on Mac: get the error on screen explained, dictate long prompts into Cursor and write commit messages by voice.
targetKeyword: voice assistant for developers on mac
intro: Lazur is a voice assistant for developers on the Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what the error on screen means, where a setting lives, or for a commit message. Hold fn to talk long prompts into your coding agent.
tldr: “What does this error mean?” with the stack trace on screen, answered out loud.
Talk long prompts into Cursor or Claude Code with fn.
“Write a commit message for this” with the diff open.
Works in any editor and terminal.

painPoints.title: Errors and unfamiliar code
painPoints.text: Copying a stack trace into a chat window, then explaining what you were doing.

painPoints.title: Prompts got long
painPoints.text: Good agent prompts carry context. Typing all of it is where people cut corners.

painPoints.title: Settings you use twice a year
painPoints.text: Signing certificates, build settings, cloud consoles.

day.result: Reads the trace on screen and explains it.
Points at Signing & Capabilities in Xcode.

day.say: write a commit message for this
search the docs for useEffect cleanup

demo.result: The port is already in use. Another dev server is running on 3000. Stop it or start this one on 3001.

blocks.text: Next to your coding agent, not instead of it
Lazur does not edit your code. Your agent does that. Lazur explains what is on screen, types your prompts by voice and handles the small stuff. See [Lazur in Cursor](/apps/cursor).

faq.question: Does Lazur work in every app?
faq.answer: Yes. It works on top of any Mac app: Mail, Slack, Chrome, Word, Figma, Cursor and the rest.

faq.question: Is it always listening?
faq.answer: No. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot are not stored.
